error.title: The interface hit an error
error.safe: Your files, settings and running tasks are not affected. Try again first; if that does not help, try the other options in order.
error.resetNote: Restoring the default interface only resets the look and layout. No data is deleted.
error.hint: When reporting the problem, please include the text below.
error.copyFailed: Copy failed. Please select the text and copy it manually

overview.title: TRM UI
overview.whatBody:
A set of design tokens, a component library, eight-language i18n, a sidebar app shell, and a build setup that runs as-is.
The whole src/trm/ directory depends on no product code and can be copied out directly.
overview.whyBody:
Every new product starts from the same interface: the same tokens, the same components, the same motion.
Improvements come back here too, instead of scattering into diverging copies inside each product.
overview.rule1: Every colour comes from a token. A hard-coded colour is always wrong in the other theme, and the error is only visible when someone switches.
overview.rule2: Every string comes from a locale pack. All eight are forced into the same shape by a build-time check, not by good intentions.
overview.rule3: src/trm/ imports nothing outside itself. The moment it reaches into product code, the template degrades into “part of one product”.
overview.themeTip: “Follow system” writes no data-theme and relies on prefers-color-scheme; picking light or dark stamps the attribute onto <html>.
overview.langTip: All eight packs are bundled at build time, so switching is a synchronous swap. Raw keys never flash before the text appears.

shell.title: Desktop shell
shell.web: This is the web preview. Window buttons, the tray and saving the config all need the desktop app. In a browser they are not shown, raise no errors and never pretend to work.
shell.sourceTip: The UI is served over a custom protocol, so a frontend/ directory next to the exe can replace the shipped copy. Without this item, a misapplied UI patch is invisible, and the user can only report that something broke after the update.
shell.autostartTip: The registry is the source of truth, not the config file. Config records product settings, while autostart is a fact about this machine. If they were mixed, copying the config to another machine would show the switch on while nothing actually starts. Windows only.

components.sub: Everything below is a live control, not a screenshot.
components.buttonsNote: A busy button must not just go grey: grey is a state, the moving dots are the receipt. Without them, “working” and “didn’t register my click” look identical.
components.segmentNote: One thumb that slides, not a separate background painted under each button. The first looks like one object moving. The second looks like one light going out and another coming on, which is two flickers.

field.name: Display name
field.nameTip: The help mark has to be a button that handles its own click. It often sits inside a label, and a label forwards clicks to the control it owns.
field.deviceDesc: A saved option that has left the list stays visible and is marked as unavailable. An empty box would suggest it was never set.
field.volumeNote: While dragging, the knob is drawn at the pointer’s real position with no transition. It glides onto the step only when you let go, and that movement shows which step you actually got.

list.item1Body:
Anything that looks clickable must be clickable. This row once had only the styling, and no onClick was wired. People clicked it four times, nothing happened, and they concluded the app was broken.

The styling now follows whether an onClick exists, not a separate clickable flag.
list.item2: Anything can go on the right

type.sub: Body is 15px at 1.65 line-height. The size steps are fixed. Do not add a new value between them.

color.sub: Switch to dark and look again: every swatch has to hold up in both themes.

motion.sub: Page direction follows the nav order. Click a few tabs above and you’ll see it.
motion.easeNav: Page transitions only. It starts fast, ends slowly and never overshoots. The page layer sits flush with the window edge, so an overshoot would show a visible seam.
motion.spring: For small elements. It overshoots, so it is used only on elements that do not touch the window edge, such as the segment thumb and floating panels.
motion.ease: The general-purpose transition. Hover, press, colour changes.
motion.easeSoft: Gentle start and slow settle, for fades and small moves
motion.springSettle: Critically damped spring with no overshoot, for large morphs
motion.springGentle: About 1% overshoot, for page changes and small moves
motion.springBouncy: About 8% overshoot, for small scale changes only
motion.flowSub: Finished but unseen: only a streak of light runs past
motion.flightSub: Click a small window: it flies to the middle and grows, and the middle one shrinks into the free slot.
motion.nudgeBody: It rises in from below; when closed its height folds away and the content below moves up.
motion.modalBody: It lifts and grows slightly on open; on close it plays its exit before it is removed, instead of vanishing.
motion.drawerBody: It slides in from the right to show details without leaving the page.

patterns.sub: Patterns that recur in desktop apps. Every one is live.
patterns.warnLine: Needs 14 GB of VRAM; this machine has 12 GB
patterns.modalText: Click outside or press Esc to close; closing is animated too.
patterns.drawerText: Slides in from the right so details open without leaving the page.

inter.sub: In-page switching, comments, step guides, prompts, errors, ring charts, panels and a floating button
inter.c1: The instructions are clear; it worked the first time.
inter.c2: On a slower computer it takes a while.
inter.stepBody: Each step does one thing; choose Next when it’s done.
inter.notice1: Report problems on the issue page.
inter.notice2: Generate a diagnostic package and attach it before you submit.

set.sub: Three kinds of settings: appearance, general and shortcuts. Labels on the left, controls on the right, notes below. A change that needs a restart shows a bar at the top.
set.wallpaperNote: A still image. Very large images slow down loading.
set.bannerHint: Leave empty to use the default.
set.compatTip: Turn on if the window shows garbled or blank areas. Takes effect after a restart.
set.prewarmDesc: Uses some graphics memory in advance so work can start sooner.
set.statsDesc: Sends only a random anonymous ID, the app version and the hardware acceleration in use. Nothing that identifies you.
set.mouseDesc: Button 4 goes back and button 5 goes forward. In this demo it moves between the pages on the left.
set.restartBody: Compatible rendering was changed. Restart the app to apply it.
set.keysHint: Click a shortcut, then press new keys. Esc cancels and Backspace clears it. If another action already uses the keys, that action's shortcut is cleared and you are told.
set.globalTip: When checked it works in any app, but no other app can use the keys. When unchecked it works only while this app is in front.
set.moved: {combo} was used for "{from}". "{from}" now has no shortcut.

more.boardSub: Sources on the left, the list in the middle, the selected item's editor on the right, and what is running fixed at the bottom.
more.editNote: Name, number, range and shortcuts are edited here; the list stays put.
more.editEmpty: Select an item in the list to edit it here.
more.effectLogs: Earlier records will be unavailable for troubleshooting
more.effectTrash: Deleted items can no longer be restored
more.effectResume: You can no longer resume from where you stopped
more.effectRedo: You will need to process again from the start
more.starterSub: When nothing is installed yet, offer a few right away: one click downloads, progress shows in place, and it can be cancelled.

text.sub: How interface text is written, with a wrong and a right example for each rule.
